vehicleWarranty.eyebrow: CASE STUDY  ·  NSA AND TRUE AIM
vehicleWarranty.title: The same claims decisions, made in a fraction of the time.
vehicleWarranty.summary: How NSA transferred the reasoning and decisioning of its claims experts into True Aim software and reduced the work on a complex claim by 86%.

facts.label: Markets
facts.value: Switzerland, Germany, Austria and other European countries

startingPoint.heading: The starting point
startingPoint.text: NSA assesses many thousands of vehicle warranty claims every year. Every claim requires a careful coverage check, and that requires real expertise. The administration around it takes longer than the decision itself. A claim arrives as up to five documents, across around 50 vehicle brands and 14 document types. Every item and its price is filed, labelled and re-keyed into the claims system by hand.
startingPoint.calloutText: from True Aim’s first test on real NSA claim files to a working system in the hands of NSA’s claims team.

solution.heading: What the solution does
solution.intro: NSA’s claims experts set out exactly how they decide a claim. True Aim hard-coded those rules into its decision engine and tested them against real NSA claims. The engine now makes the routine decisions the way the experts would, records the reason for each one and refers anything requiring judgement to a person.

items.title: Reads the documents.
items.desc: Every labour and parts item is captured with its price, directly from the repair estimate. Nothing is filed, labelled or re-keyed by hand.

items.title: Decides coverage.
items.desc: NSA’s own rules are applied line by line, with the policy clause recorded behind every decision.

items.title: Drafts the response.
items.desc: The customer response is returned ready for review.

items.title: Refers judgement calls.
items.desc: Anything outside the rules goes to an expert, with the file already prepared.

claimTypes.heading: Two kinds of claim
claimTypes.intro: A claim is not a single unit of work, so the saving is not uniform.
claimTypes.simple: A simple claim involves one part, one cause and one clear answer. NSA’s experts can decide it quickly. The time is consumed by the administration around it.
claimTypes.complex: A complex claim carries several parts and labour items, and each line has to be tested against the policy: included, excluded, wear, pre-existing or outside the term. That is where the expert hours are spent, and that is where the engine contributes most.
claimTypes.mix: NSA’s book of claims comprises 73% simple claims and 27% complex claims.

timeSaving.heading: Time saving per claim
rows: Document handling, filing, labelling and re-keying
Writing the response to the customer
timeSaving.footnote: *Document capture is fully automated, from the moment a claim arrives through the online form or by email. The time shown is the expert’s confirmation of items the engine flags for verification, typically a low-quality scan, a handwritten amendment on an estimate or a part description that does not match a known catalogue entry. On a clean file there is nothing to review.
timeSaving.summary: That is 83% less work on a simple claim and 86% less on a complex one. Document review takes a little longer on a complex claim because there are more documents and more line items, so more items are surfaced for confirmation. Every line not flagged already carries its decision and the policy clause supporting it.

book.heading: What that means across the book of claims
rows: Handling time on an average claim
Time to answer a claim, start to finish
total: Claim volume the same team can assess
book.basis: Basis. Weighted on NSA’s claim mix of 73% simple and 27% complex. Time to answer a claim covers the full process including follow-ups and handovers, which True Aim does not change.

expertise.title: More time for expertise.
expertise.text: Experts spend their day on the claims where the answer is a judgement rather than a lookup.

sameDecision.heading: The same decision, every time
sameDecision.text: True Aim assesses every claim against the same rules and with the same care, whatever the time of day or the workload. Two identical claims receive the same answer. Every decision records the document, the page and the policy clause it rests on, so any claim can be explained later.

collaboration.heading: The collaboration
collaboration.text: True Aim moved from the first test to a working system in seven days. NSA’s experts handed over their rules directly and saw them operating in the system the same week.
collaboration.next: Next: further claim categories, more line items and document types, wider vehicle brand coverage and the move from pilot scope into the standard claims process.

vehicleWarranty.method: Based on time measurements of every process step on real NSA claims, both in the current process and in tests with True Aim, split by claim complexity. Claim mix is NSA’s own. Figures are rounded to the nearest minute.
